mainTopic: Mistakes in the עמידה, the meaning of קבע, short prayers in danger, and תפלת הדרך
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer about someone who forgot to ask for rain: he goes back to the start only if he remembers after שומע תפלה. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that someone who forgot יעלה ויבא on ראש חודש goes back to עבודה, unless he already finished, in which case he starts over. רב פפא, citing a tradition from רב, explains that 'finished' means he already moved his feet. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds, in two versions, that it also depends on whether he usually says תחנונים after davening. The גמרא then explains רבי אליעזר's word קבע in the משנה in several ways: a burden, not said as a plea, nothing new added, or not praying at דמדומי חמה. Praying at that time is a מצוה, but in ארץ ישראל they cursed it for fear of missing the time. Next comes the meaning of פרשת העבור and several versions of the short prayer for a dangerous place, and רב הונא rules like אחרים. Finally, אליהו's advice leads to the obligation and full text of תפלת הדרך, and אביי begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Going back to the start applies only after passing שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: This is the last line of an answer that began on the previous amud. The ruling that one who forgot to ask for rain returns to the beginning applies only when he remembers after finishing שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling that he goes back to the start is talking about a case where he remembered only after the ברכה of 'Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes resolving a contradiction about someone who forgot to ask for rain. Going back to the start applies only if he remembers after שומע תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulings seemed to clash. One says he can add the rain request in שומע תפלה. The other says he goes back to the beginning. The answer splits the cases: before finishing שומע תפלה he can still add it there, but after that the chance is gone, so he restarts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who hears prayer', the last of the middle (request) ברכות of the עמידה

steps.whatToRemember: Forgot to ask for rain? You can still add it in שומע תפלה. Once you have passed שומע תפלה, you go back to the beginning.

phrases.english: This [case] is where he remembered after 'Who hears prayer.'
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to the ruling that he returns to the beginning; the other half of the answer came just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאִדְּכַר בָּתַר שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the resolution begun on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בכך, הא בכך): before versus after שומע תפלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings about forgetting the rain request seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going back to the start applies only once he has passed שומע תפלה.

steps.title: Forgetting יעלה ויבא on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules: if someone forgot the ראש חודש addition in עבודה and remembers during עבודה, הודאה, or שים שלום, he goes back to עבודה. If he already finished, he goes back to the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said in the name of רב אסי, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: If someone mistakenly did not mention ראש חודש in the ברכה of עבודה, he goes back to עבודה. If he remembers in הודאה, he goes back to עבודה. If he remembers in שים שלום, he goes back to עבודה. If he already finished, he goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule, related to the last one, about forgetting יעלה ויבא on ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as he is still inside the עמידה, he only goes back to the ברכה where the addition belongs (עבודה) and continues from there. Once he has completed the whole עמידה, the fix is to start the עמידה over.

keyTerms.meaning: the New Month, when יעלה ויבא is added
the ברכה of רצה, about the Temple service
he goes back to the beginning

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said that Rav Asi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: If one erred and did not mention [the addition] of the New Month
in 'Service', he returns to 'Service'.
phrases.notes: 'Service' is the ברכה of רצה, where יעלה ויבא goes.

phrases.english: If he remembered in 'Thanksgiving', he returns to 'Service'.
In 'Grant peace', he returns to 'Service'.
And if he finished, he returns to the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, parallel rule about forgetting an addition in the עמידה, this time for ראש חודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While still in the עמידה, he goes back to עבודה. Once he has finished, he restarts from the beginning.

steps.title: 'Finished' means he already moved his feet
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the rule 'if he finished, he goes back to the beginning' to someone who already moved his feet. If he has not moved them, he only goes back to עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא son of רב אחא בר אדא said: When we said 'if he finished he goes back to the beginning', we meant only where he already moved his feet. But if he did not move his feet, he goes back to עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains exactly what 'finished' means in the previous rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the last words of the עמידה is not yet considered 'finished' for this rule. As long as he has not moved his feet away, he is still connected to his prayer. So he can still go back to עבודה instead of starting over.

keyTerms.meaning: he uprooted (moved) his feet, stepping away at the end of the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'finished' as simply saying the last ברכה. Here it means finishing and also moving your feet.
steps.whatToRemember: Forgot יעלה ויבא and have not yet moved your feet? Go back to רצה. Already moved your feet? Start the עמידה again.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa son of Rav Acha bar Adda said:
That which we said, 'if he finished, he returns to the beginning',
we only said it where he moved his feet,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא עָקַר רַגְלָיו — חוֹזֵר לָעֲבוֹדָה.
phrases.english: but if he did not move his feet, he returns to 'Service'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן סִייֵּם חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the last clause of רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going back to the beginning applies only after he has moved his feet. Before that, he goes back to עבודה.

steps.title: Where did you get this from?
steps.stepSummary: Someone asks רב פפא for the source of his limitation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks רב פפא how he knows his rule about moving the feet. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about where the ruling came from, not about its logic. In other words: is this your own idea, or did you receive it from a teacher?

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you have this?

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you have this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מְנָא לָךְ הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רב פפא's rule about moving the feet.

steps.title: From my father, who heard it from רב
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that he heard it from his father, who heard it from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it from my father, my teacher, and my father, my teacher, heard it from רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא names his source: a tradition passed down from רב through his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not his own reasoning. It is a received tradition going back to the great אמורא רב, which gives it strong authority.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'moved his feet' limit is an accepted tradition from רב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵאַבָּא מָרִי שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it from my father, my teacher,
and my father, my teacher, [heard it] from Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מֵאַבָּא מָרִי שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tradition: from רב, to רב פפא's father, to רב פפא.

steps.title: First version: someone who usually says supplications goes back only to עבודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק limits the rule "if he moved his feet, he goes back to the beginning" to someone who does not usually say תחנונים after davening. Someone who does usually say them only goes back to עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What we said, that if he moved his feet he goes back to the beginning, applies only to someone who does not usually say supplications after his prayer. But if he usually says supplications after his prayer, he goes back only to עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a new limit to the rule from Step 3: moving your feet does not always send you back to the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, moving the feet meant the תפלה was over, so he started again. רב נחמן בר יצחק says this is only true for someone who does not add supplications afterward. For someone who usually adds them, the תפלה still counts as unfinished, so he goes back only to עבודה. This version is lenient: it lets more people avoid starting over.

keyTerms.meaning: He moved his feet, the step back that marks the end of the עמידה
Personal supplications or requests added after the תפלה
Accustomed, someone who usually does something
We only said it in a case where (a formula that limits an earlier rule)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן עָקַר רַגְלָיו חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ
phrases.english: That which we said, that if he moved his feet he returns to the beginning,
we only said it where he is not accustomed
to say supplications after his prayer,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רָגִיל לוֹמַר תַּחֲנוּנִים אַחַר תְּפִלָּתוֹ
phrases.english: but if he is accustomed to say supplications after his prayer,
he returns to the blessing of עבודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן עָקַר רַגְלָיו חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to רב פפא's rule about moving the feet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who moved his feet but usually says תחנונים after davening goes back only to עבודה, not to the beginning.

steps.title: Second version: someone who does not usually say supplications goes back to the beginning
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב נחמן בר יצחק limits the opposite rule. Going back only to עבודה before moving the feet applies only to someone who usually says תחנונים. Someone who does not goes back to the beginning even if he has not moved his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What we said, that if he did not move his feet he goes back to עבודה, applies only to someone who usually says supplications after his prayer. But if he does not usually say supplications after his prayer, he goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of what רב נחמן בר יצחק said. In this report his limit is placed on the other half of רב פפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, he limits the lenient rule "he did not move his feet, so he goes back to עבודה." That rule works only for someone who usually adds supplications. If he does not add them, finishing the תפלה already counts as the end, even without moving his feet, so he starts over. This version is stricter than the first.

keyTerms.meaning: To the beginning of the תפלה

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same idea, whether he usually says תחנונים, but they apply it to different halves of the rule. The first version makes the "moved his feet" rule easier. The second makes the "did not move his feet" rule stricter.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן כִּי לֹא עָקַר רַגְלָיו חוֹזֵר לַעֲבוֹדָה
phrases.english: That which we said, that when he did not move his feet he returns to עבודה,
we only said it where he is accustomed
to say supplications after his prayer,
but if he is not accustomed

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר תַּחֲנוּנִים אַחַר תְּפִלָּתוֹ — חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: to say supplications after his prayer, he returns to the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of Step 6 that applies the same idea to the other half of רב פפא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who has not moved his feet but does not usually say תחנונים goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a person usually adds תחנונים after davening decides whether his תפלה counts as finished. The first version uses this to be lenient after moving the feet. The second uses it to be strict before moving the feet.

steps.title: What does "קבע" mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה about one who makes his תפלה קבע, and asks what "קבע" means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי אליעזר says: Whoever makes his prayer fixed, and so on. What does "fixed" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the meaning of one word. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said that if someone's תפלה is קבע, it is not a real supplication. The word "קבע" is not clear: it could describe his attitude, how he speaks, or what he says. The next three steps each give a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed or set: a תפלה said in a fixed way, without real asking
And so on: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Whoever makes his prayer fixed, and so on.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה says: his prayer is not a real supplication.

phrases.english: What is "fixed"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא goes back to explain another part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word "קבע" in רבי אליעזר's statement.

steps.title: First answer: a prayer that feels like a burden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי, quoting רבי אושעיא, explains that קבע means someone who feels his תפלה is a burden on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי אושעיא: Anyone whose prayer feels to him like a heavy load.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first explanation of "קבע": it is about the person's attitude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, "קבע" means davening as a fixed duty that he wants to get done. Someone who sees his תפלה as a load to get rid of is not truly asking.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems to him, it feels to him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Anyone whose prayer seems to him like a burden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁתְּפִלָּתוֹ דּוֹמָה עָלָיו כְּמַשּׂוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבע means a תפלה that feels like a burden to the one davening.

steps.title: Second answer: not praying in the language of supplication
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that קבע means someone who does not say his תפלה in the language of supplication.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: Anyone who does not say it in the language of supplication.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second explanation of "קבע": it is about the way he speaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is not how he feels but how the words come out. If he just recites the words without saying them as a request, his תפלה is קבע.

keyTerms.meaning: In the language of supplication, the way one pleads for something

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּחֲנוּנִים.
phrases.english: Anyone who does not say it in the language of supplication.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּחֲנוּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of Step 8, different from Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבע means a תפלה not said in the language of supplication.

steps.title: Third answer: unable to add anything new
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both explain that קבע means someone who cannot add anything new to his תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: Anyone who is not able to add something new in it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third explanation of "קבע": it is about what he says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, "קבע" means saying only the fixed words, exactly the same each time. A person who cannot add anything new or personal to his תפלה has made it קבע.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר.
phrases.english: Anyone who is not able to add something new in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבע means a תפלה to which one cannot add anything new.
steps.whatToRemember: Three explanations of קבע: (1) the תפלה feels like a burden, (2) it is not said as a supplication, (3) nothing new can be added to it.

steps.title: רבי זירא: I could add something new, but I am afraid of getting confused
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he is able to add something new to his תפלה, but he is afraid he might get confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I am able to add something new to it, but I am afraid that I might get confused.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא responds to the last explanation, the one about adding something new, with his own experience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said a person should be able to add something new to his תפלה. רבי זירא says he could do it, but he holds back because adding new words might confuse him. This shows that adding something new carries a real risk.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
I am able to add something new in it,
but I am afraid that perhaps I will get confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא יָכֵילְנָא לְחַדּוֹשֵׁי בַּהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A personal comment on the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא could add something new to his תפלה but does not, because he is afraid of getting confused.

steps.title: Fixed prayer means not praying at sunrise or sunset glow
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין explain that קבע means someone who does not pray at דמדומי חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The brothers אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין both said: קבע means anyone who does not pray with the reddening of the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question from Step 8 about what קבע means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers looked at a person's attitude or the words of his prayer. This answer looks at timing. Someone who does not make the effort to pray at the special time of sunrise or sunset is called קבע.

keyTerms.meaning: The reddish glow of the sun, right at sunrise and right before sunset

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin
who both said:
anyone who does not pray
phrases.notes: This is their explanation of the word קבע from the משנה.

phrases.english: with the reddening of the sun.
phrases.notes: The sun's reddish glow just as it rises and just before it sets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth explanation of קבע, after the ones in Steps 9-11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבע means someone who does not pray at דמדומי חמה.

steps.title: It is a מצוה to pray at sunrise and sunset glow
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: it is a מצוה to pray at דמדומי חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is a מצוה to pray with the reddening of the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last answer by showing that praying at דמדומי חמה is a real מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 would make no sense unless this time were special. רבי יוחנן's statement shows that it is, so a person who skips it is missing something important.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment or a good deed one should do

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a מצוה to pray
with the reddening of the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 13 by showing that this time of prayer is a מצוה.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that קבע means not praying at דמדומי חמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that praying at דמדומי חמה is a מצוה

steps.title: The verse behind praying with the sun
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives the פסוק that hints to praying at דמדומי חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: What is the פסוק for this? "Let them fear You with the sun and before the moon, generation after generation."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a פסוק that is the source for רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fearing ה׳ is shown through prayer. The words "with the sun" and "before the moon" hint that prayer should be close to sunrise and close to sunset.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
What is the verse for this?
"Let them fear You with the sun
and before the moon, generation after generation."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה to pray at דמדומי חמה

steps.title: In the Land of Israel they cursed those who prayed at sunset glow
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they cursed someone who prays at דמדומי חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they cursed anyone who prays with the reddening of the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a surprising opposite view: in ארץ ישראל they were strongly against praying at this time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after praising prayer at דמדומי חמה, the גמרא reports that people in ארץ ישראל cursed it. This sets up the next question: why would they be so harsh?
steps.confusionAlert: This does not erase רבי יוחנן's מצוה. The concern is about waiting until the very last moment before sunset, as the next steps explain.

phrases.english: In the West they cursed
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: anyone who prays
with the reddening of the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָיְיטִי עֲלַהּ בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a view that seems to go against Steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל they cursed someone who prays at דמדומי חמה.

steps.title: Why curse such a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why they cursed this person. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since praying at this time is a מצוה, a curse seems very strange. The גמרא needs to explain what is wrong with it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would someone praying at דמדומי חמה deserve a curse?

steps.title: He might miss the time
steps.stepSummary: The reason: he might get mixed up about the time, and the time for prayer will pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the time will slip by him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a person who waits until sunset might lose track of the time and miss the prayer completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the time itself but the risk. Someone cutting it so close to sunset could easily let the time run out. So both views can be true: it is a מצוה, but it is dangerous to wait for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The time gets mixed up for him and slips away

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sides to praying at דמדומי חמה: it is a special מצוה (רבי יוחנן), but in ארץ ישראל they cursed it because a person might miss the time.

phrases.english: Perhaps the time will get mixed up for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא מִיטַּרְפָא לֵיהּ שַׁעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may lose track of the time, and the time for prayer will pass.

steps.title: What does פרשת העבור mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's short prayer from the משנה and asks what פרשת העבור means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: One who walks in a dangerous place prays a short prayer, and so on, "in every פרשת העבור." What does "פרשת העבור" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the short prayer for a dangerous place, and asks about one unclear phrase in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words פרשת העבור are hard to understand. The גמרא asks for their meaning before explaining them in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A phrase in the prayer whose meaning the גמרא now explains

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
One who walks in a dangerous place
prays a short prayer, etc.
"in every parashat ha'ibur."
What is "parashat ha'ibur"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״פָּרָשַׁת הָעִבּוּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase פרשת העבור in רבי יהושע's prayer.

steps.title: Even when You are full of anger at them
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא explains: even when ה׳ is filled with anger (עברה) at them like a pregnant woman (עוברה), may their needs be before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: Even at a time when You are filled with anger at them like a pregnant woman is filled, may all their needs be before You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains פרשת העבור as a time when ה׳ is full of anger at the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עבור is read as two words at once: עברה (anger) and עוברה (a pregnant woman). Just as a pregnant woman is full, ה׳ is "full" of anger, and even then we ask Him to care for our needs.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva:
Even at a time
when You are filled with anger at them
like a pregnant woman
phrases.notes: A play on the word עבור: it sounds like עברה (anger) and also like עוברה (pregnant).

phrases.english: may all their needs be before You.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרשת העבור means a time when ה׳ is filled with anger (עברה) like a pregnant woman (עוברה).

steps.title: Even when they break the Torah
steps.stepSummary: A second version of מר עוקבא's explanation: even when they transgress (עוברים) the Torah, may their needs be before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: Even at a time when they transgress the words of the Torah, may all their needs be before You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of מר עוקבא's explanation of פרשת העבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here עבור is read as עוברים, "transgressing." Instead of ה׳'s anger, the focus is on the people's sins. Even then, we ask ה׳ to take care of their needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Transgressing the words of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: פרשת העבור comes from the word עבור. One version reads it as ה׳'s anger (עברה); the other reads it as the people's sins (עוברים). Either way, we pray that their needs be met.

phrases.english: Some say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: that Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva:
Even at a time when they transgress
the words of the Torah
may all their needs be before You.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the answer in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרשת העבור means a time when they transgress (עוברים) the Torah.

steps.title: A teaching about the short prayer in a dangerous place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone walking among packs of wild animals and robbers says a short prayer, and asks what that prayer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who walks in a place of packs of wild animals and robbers prays a short prayer. And which is the short prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives more versions of the short prayer. This line sets up the opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave רבי יהושע's version. The ברייתא names the danger more clearly, wild animals and robbers, and asks for the exact words. The answers follow in the next two steps.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who walks in a place of packs of wild animals and robbers
prays a short prayer.
And which is the short prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְקוֹם גְּדוּדֵי חַיָּה וְלִסְטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same topic as the משנה's short prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place of wild animals and robbers, one says a short prayer.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's short prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's version: Do Your will above, give peace of mind to those who fear You below, do what is good in Your eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: "Do Your will in the heavens above, give peace of mind to those who fear You below, and do what is good in Your eyes. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives his words for the short prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His prayer does not list specific requests. It asks ה׳ to do His will and what is good in His eyes, while giving calm to those who fear Him. It ends with the ברכה "שומע תפלה."

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Do Your will in the heavens above,
and give peace of mind to those who fear You below,
and do what is good in Your eyes.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עֲשֵׂה רְצוֹנְךָ בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The short prayer is: עשה רצונך בשמים ממעל, ending with שומע תפלה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's short prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע's version: Hear the cry of Your nation ישראל and quickly fulfill their request.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: "Hear the cry of Your nation ישראל, and quickly fulfill their request. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a different set of words for the short prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע asks directly and urgently for the people's requests to be answered quickly. It also ends with "שומע תפלה."
steps.whatToRemember: There are several versions of the short prayer for a dangerous place: רבי יהושע's in the משנה, and in the ברייתא those of רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק and אחרים (Steps 23-26). All of them end with "שומע תפלה."

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
"Hear the cry of Your nation Israel,
and quickly fulfill their request.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שְׁמַע שַׁוְעַת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the ברייתא's question, different from רבי אליעזר's in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The short prayer is: שמע שועת עמך ישראל, ending with שומע תפלה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's version of the short prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק gives his wording for the short prayer and closes it with the ברכה 'שומע תפלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: 'Hear the cry of Your nation ישראל, and quickly fulfill their request. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer to the ברייתא's question about which short prayer to say in a dangerous place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wording is almost the same as רבי יהושע's version in Step 24, which also ends with 'ברוך אתה ה׳ שומע תפלה'. The only difference is one word: he says צעקת ('shout') where רבי יהושע said שועת ('cry').

keyTerms.meaning: Who hears prayer: the closing of the ברכה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
'Hear the cry of Your nation Israel,'
'and quickly fulfill their request.'
'Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question in Step 22, differing from רבי יהושע's wording by one word (צעקת instead of שועת).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The short prayer is 'שמע צעקת עמך ישראל ועשה מהרה בקשתם', ending with 'ברוך אתה ה׳ שומע תפלה'.

steps.title: The version of אחרים: many needs, limited understanding
steps.stepSummary: אחרים give a fuller version that admits Israel's needs are many, asks ה׳ to supply each person's needs, and ends with 'שומע תפלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: 'The needs of Your nation ישראל are many and their understanding is short. May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, to give each and every one enough for his livelihood, and to each and every body what it lacks. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion, called אחרים ('others'), gives its own wording for the short prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of asking ה׳ to answer what the people request, this version admits that people can't even fully say what they need. So it asks ה׳ to provide what each person and each body truly lacks.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': an unnamed תנא or group of תנאים
Their understanding is short or limited

phrases.english: Others say:
'The needs of Your nation Israel are many'
'and their understanding is short.'
'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתִּתֵּן לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כְּדֵי פַרְנָסָתוֹ,
phrases.english: 'to give each and every one enough for his livelihood,'
'and to each and every body whatever it lacks.'
'Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to Step 22, with a different idea: ask for what people truly need, not only what they request.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The short prayer is 'צרכי עמך ישראל מרובין ודעתם קצרה, יהי רצון', ending with 'שומע תפלה'.

steps.title: The halacha follows the version of אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה follows אחרים' wording of the short prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the versions have been listed, רב הונא decides which one we actually say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of every wording brought from Step 22 onward, the practical ruling picks אחרים' version, the one that starts 'צרכי עמך ישראל מרובין'.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: The short prayer said in a dangerous place follows אחרים: 'צרכי עמך ישראל מרובין ודעתם קצרה'.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha follows Others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between all the versions just listed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We say the short prayer in the wording of אחרים.

steps.title: אליהו's advice: don't get angry, don't get drunk, consult your Creator before traveling
steps.stepSummary: אליהו tells רב יהודה three pieces of advice, the last being to consult with his Creator before setting out on a journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to רב יהודה, brother of רב סלא חסידא: Don't get angry and you won't sin. Don't get drunk and you won't sin. And when you set out on the road, consult with your Creator and then go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from prayers in danger to a related topic, prayer for travelers. It quotes אליהו's advice, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two lines warn against anger and drunkenness, two things that lead a person to sin. The third line is the one the גמרא focuses on: before a trip you should 'consult with your Creator,' and the next step asks what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't boil over, meaning don't get angry

phrases.english: Eliyahu said to Rav Yehuda,
the brother of Rav Sala the pious:
Don't get angry, and you won't sin.
Don't get drunk, and you won't sin.
And when you set out on the road,
consult with your Creator, and then go out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic linked to the previous one: from prayers in danger to prayer before travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before setting out on a trip, one should 'consult with his Creator'.

steps.title: What does 'consult with your Creator' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אליהו meant by 'consult with your Creator and go out'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'consult with your Creator and go out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of אליהו's unclear phrase, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How do you 'consult' with ה׳ in practice? The phrase is vague, so the גמרא wants to know what action it actually requires.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is 'consult with your Creator and go out'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִמָּלֵךְ בְּקוֹנְךָ וָצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last line of אליהו's advice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical action 'consulting with your Creator' before a trip refers to.

steps.title: It means תפלת הדרך
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב in the name of רב חסדא explains that 'consulting with your Creator' means saying תפלת הדרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: This is the traveler's prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: 'consulting with your Creator' means saying the traveler's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You 'consult' with ה׳ by praying to Him before the trip. So אליהו's advice is really pointing to תפלת הדרך.

keyTerms.meaning: The traveler's prayer, said when setting out on a journey

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said in the name of Rav Chisda:
This is the traveler's prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: זוֹ תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Consult with your Creator' means saying תפלת הדרך.

steps.title: Everyone who travels must say תפלת הדרך
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that anyone setting out on a journey is required to say תפלת הדרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: Anyone who sets out on the road must pray the traveler's prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement from the same speakers turns אליהו's good advice into a clear obligation for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו's words could have sounded like personal advice to one person, רב יהודה. רב חסדא makes it a general rule: every traveler must say תפלת הדרך.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets out on a journey

steps.whatToRemember: תפלת הדרך is required of every traveler, and it comes from אליהו's advice to 'consult with your Creator' before leaving.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical obligation of תפלת הדרך.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov said in the name of Rav Chisda:
Anyone who sets out on the road
must pray the traveler's prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כׇּל הַיּוֹצֵא לַדֶּרֶךְ צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying תפלת הדרך, the same speakers set it as a binding rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person setting out on a journey is obligated to say תפלת הדרך.

steps.title: What are the words of the traveler's prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact wording of תפלת הדרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the traveler's prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just learned that a traveler must say תפלת הדרך, so it now asks what the words of that prayer are. This question sets up the next step, where the full text is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that you must say a prayer is not enough. You also need to know what to say. The question moves from 'is it required?' to 'what exactly is it?'

keyTerms.meaning: The traveler's prayer, said when setting out on a journey

phrases.english: What is the traveler's prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב חסדא's ruling in step 31 by asking for the text of the required prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of תפלת הדרך.

steps.title: The full text of the traveler's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the complete wording of תפלת הדרך, ending with the blessing 'שומע תפלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that You lead me in peace, direct my steps in peace, and support me in peace. Save me from every enemy and ambusher on the way. Send blessing to the work of my hands. Let me find grace, kindness and compassion in Your eyes and in the eyes of everyone who sees me. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the whole prayer word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer asks for three things: a safe journey (peace, and rescue from enemies and ambushes), success (blessing on one's work), and favor with ה׳ and people. It closes with a ברכה, 'שומע תפלה'.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be Your will (a common way to open a request to ה׳)
Enemy and ambusher (someone hiding in wait to attack)
Who hears prayer (the closing words of the ברכה)

steps.whatToRemember: תפלת הדרך asks for a peaceful journey, protection from danger, blessing in one's work, and favor in ה׳'s eyes and people's eyes. It ends with 'ברוך אתה ה׳ שומע תפלה'.

phrases.english: May it be Your will, Lord my God,
that You lead me to peace,
and direct my steps to peace,
and support me to peace,
and rescue me from the hand of every enemy
and ambusher on the way,
and send blessing to the work of my hands,
and grant me grace, kindness, and compassion
in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me.
Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 32 by giving the prayer's text.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The full wording of תפלת הדרך, from 'יהי רצון' to 'שומע תפלה'.

steps.title: אביי begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a statement with the word 'לעולם' ('always'). The rest continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A person should always...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. אביי begins a new teaching, but this amud ends after his first word. The rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לעולם' tells us a general rule is coming, something a person should do at all times. The next amud shows what אביי teaches and how it connects to the prayer we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: Always / at all times (opens a general rule)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Always
phrases.notes: His sentence isn't finished here. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching right after the text of תפלת הדרך is given. Its content continues past this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated on this amud. אביי's rule begins with 'לעולם' and continues on the next amud.
